blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Я провела ___ (неделя) с палестинской семьей из Газы.
exercises.prompt: I spent a week with a Palestinian family from Gaza.
exercises.why: The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену. Я жду письма.* — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The accusative case is used to denote the direct object of the preceding verb and answers the questions кого? — whom? or что? — what?» — DLI, Lesson 18.
exercises.context: The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену.

exercises.why: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. — Я не пью молока. Я вижу реку. — Я не вижу реки.* The verb ждать takes no preposition. The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену. Я жду письма.* The genitive case is used to denote an indefinite quantity of something: *Дайте воды, молока, хлеба.* Several masculine nouns may take the ending -у, -ю (instead of -а, -я) in the genitive case when a quantity is expressed: *Дайте, пожалуйста, супу, сахару, чаю.* — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks, «Genitive case».
exercises.context: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. — Я не пью молока.

exercises.q: Сорок лет спустя они достигли ___ (земля) обетованной.
exercises.prompt: Forty years later, they reached the promised land.

Хотите стакан чаю?* — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The person or thing feared is in the Genitive case: Я боюсь этого человека.» «The object (of ждать) is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate.» — DLI, Lessons 27, 66.
